credentials.description: API key of the environment (sandbox and production keys differ, from the Dashboard)
partner ID — numeric, no leading zeros (Dashboard)

example_prompt: Check the current status of a submitted Smile ID verification by its job_id, e.g. to poll an Enhanced KYC job until it leaves 'processing'.

jobId.description: TypeID format verification identifier with 'job_' prefix. Passed as a path parameter.

status.description: Verification status. Terminal states (clear, block, attention, error) are returned with HTTP 200; processing is returned with HTTP 202; not_found is returned with HTTP 404.

user_id.description: User ID associated with the verification.

created_at.description: Timestamp the status response was generated (ISO 8601).

gotchas: Auth: mint a token with POST /v3/token, then send SmileID-Partner-ID and SmileID-Token on this request (auth.token_exchange / auth.apply). Docs (Authentication): "Access tokens expire **15 minutes** after issuance. We recommend generating a new token for every verification request rather than reusing tokens across multiple requests." Mint tokens on your backend only: the API key never goes to the browser. The endpoint's OpenAPI declares only SmileID-Token; the Authentication page requires both headers — send both.
Returns only status, job_id, user_id, message and created_at — not id_fields or the full result. The full result is delivered to your callback_url; use replay_verification_webhook to have it re-sent.
The HTTP code carries the state: 200 for a terminal status (clear, block, attention, error), 202 while processing, 404 when the job is not found or not yours. Don't treat 202 as a failure.

Observed in the sandbox (live test, 2026-10-24) — not in the docs: called right after enhanced_kyc returned 202, this endpoint answered 404 with status 'not_found', message 'Job not found' and user_id 'unknown' — the job's own created_at, as reported later in the webhook, was a few seconds after that 404. The same job_id answered 200 'clear' ('Job completed') two minutes later. A 404 right after submission does not mean the job doesn't exist: wait and retry, or rely on the callback.
jobId is the TypeID returned at submission, with the 'job_' prefix.
Keys, tokens and callback URLs are environment-specific: a sandbox token returns 401 in production.

spans: processing is returned with HTTP 202; not_found is returned with HTTP 404
TypeID format verification identifier with 'job_' prefix.
